Data source overview:  
The paper introduces the “Interactive System Optimizer” (ISO) — an RL/IRL based procedure that (1) infers reward functions from user interaction data and (2) iteratively adjusts an interactive system’s transition dynamics so that user-experienced value (expected state value) improves.  Simulated experiments confirm ISO’s effectiveness and highlight its sensitivity to reward-inference quality and the advantages of gradual, step-by-step deployment.

Report EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]  
The output follows every instruction item, all nodes inter-connect into a single fabric, no risk→intervention shortcuts are present, and JSON formatting validates.  Further guidance that distinguishes “enabled_by” vs. “enables” directionality in the canonical edge list would clarify edge semantics and reduce ambiguity during extraction.

Inference strategy justification:  
Only moderate inference was applied for two interventions (offline simulation testing and incremental deployment) that the paper implies rather than states explicitly; these edges are marked with confidence 2-3.

Extraction completeness explanation:  
All major reasoning components—mis-aligned handcrafted objectives, MDP modelling, IRL reward inference, ISO optimisation loop, experimental findings, and the deployment implications—are represented.  Each intervention node receives at least one motivating edge, and every concept node connects to the overall fabric.

Key limitations:  
1. The source uses simulation rather than real deployments, so evidence is limited (edge confidence mostly 3-4).  
2. Reward-inference algorithms beyond MaxEnt-IRL/DM-IRL are not explored, limiting generality.  
3. Only single-goal users are considered; multi-goal extensions remain open.
